utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, come in quickly please, I am running a bit behind today. What brings you in?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am pregnant and I saw another doctor but I wanted a second opinion. I have been feeling very lethargic all the time and there is a skin infection on my chest that is not going away.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. How far along is your pregnancy, and when did this skin infection start?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am six months pregnant. The infection started last summer and the skin has turned yellow in patches near the chest. The tiredness is nonstop.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any seizures, fainting, or breathlessness during this time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, no seizures thank God, but I do get breathlessness twice a day, especially in the evening. And I had one episode of seizures last summer which really scared me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned a prior episode of seizures. Any history of stroke or neurological problems in the family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My mother had a stroke some years back. As for me, nobody diagnosed me with anything like that so far.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What about cigarettes or alcohol? Are you taking any of these?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I used to have cigarettes every morning before pregnancy, but I have stopped now. Alcohol I never touched, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped. Any smoke exposure at home or work? Was any sick person around you recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, my coworker was sick a few months back with some cough and fever. And there is smoke from the kitchen stove at home.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines are you currently on? Did the previous doctor prescribe anything?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, the other doctor gave me acetaminophen for the body ache and iron supplements for my blood. I also have a thyroid problem so I take levothyroxine twice a day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you consult anyone else — any local health provider before coming here?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I went to a local informal provider near my area first. He gave me some herbal mixture but it did not help at all with the skin infection or the lethargic feeling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is there any cough or chest pain? I want to check your lung function as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: There is some chest pain on the left side of the chest. The lung area feels tight sometimes, especially at night.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me, I suspect this is a case of pulmonary infection along with hypothyroidism that is not well controlled, which is causing the lethargic feeling and the skin infection. The prior seizures episode also needs proper evaluation given your family history of stroke.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will need a X-ray of the chest — it is safe to do in pregnancy with shielding — and a stress test to rule out any cardiac involvement given your breathlessness and chest pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is the stress test safe in pregnancy? I am worried. Also should I continue the levothyroxine?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, continue your levothyroxine as before — do not skip it. We will do a modified stress test suitable for pregnancy. Your iron supplements should also continue twice a day as your blood levels are low.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the skin infection, I am prescribing a topical antibiotic cream — safe in pregnancy. Continue acetaminophen for pain but do not exceed the dose. I am also adding a pregnancy-safe iron supplements with higher dose given the lethargic state.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid any more herbal mixtures from informal providers — they can be harmful in pregnancy. Also reduce smoke exposure from the kitchen as much as possible. Avoid contact with any sick person to prevent further infection.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor, I will follow everything you said.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in — I am running a bit behind today, so let us get started quickly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Of course doctor, no problem. I was discharged two days back and they asked me to follow up with you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I have your discharge notes here. Tell me, any chest pain, shortness of breath, or dizziness since discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that. But I am getting this dull headache that comes and goes — it has been there over a year now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the headache on one side? Any nausea or light sensitivity with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes, sometimes on one side. My upper back is also paining all the time, and I feel some numbness in my toes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The one-sided dull headache with that pattern — that is likely migraine. The numbness in your toes is unlikely to be unrelated — it may be peripheral neuropathy from your diabetes.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh doctor, I have had diabetes and thyroid problem for many years. And high cholesterol also. I was also told years back I had jaundice.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. During your hospital stay, did they do a CT scan or EKG?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they did CT scan of my chest and an EKG. They also mentioned doing a bone marrow biopsy if the blood counts did not improve.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any recent family member was sick at home? Any infection exposure before the admission?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, family member was sick — my wife had fever and cough about two weeks before I got admitted.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And in the hospital they had you on dexamethasone and heparin? Were you given Tylenol for the headache as well?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, they gave me dexamethasone and heparin injections, and Tylenol for the pain. I felt a bit better but the headache is still there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you taking any herbal or alternative remedies at home alongside your regular medicines?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uh, yes doctor — I take some herbal liver tonic for my jaundice history and an herbal cholesterol supplement. I thought they are natural so no harm.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I would advise you to stop those herbal supplements for now — some of them interfere with your heparin levels and can affect liver function, especially with your past jaundice.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, I will stop them.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Do you exercise or do any physical activity regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have been doing swimming for 30 years. Even now I try to go every other day but the upper back pain is making it difficult.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is good habit, keep up the swimming once you are more stable. The upper back pain and numbness in the toes — we need your HbA1c and thyroid function test done this week so we can adjust your diabetes and thyroid medications properly.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for this migraine and the upper back pain — should I continue taking Tylenol at home?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For the migraine, I am prescribing sumatriptan — take it at the first sign of the attack. For the upper back pain, continue Tylenol as needed, and I am adding gabapentin at a low dose for the neuropathy in your toes. Also continue your statin for high cholesterol.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. One more thing — my blood sugar has been fluctuating all the time since the past month.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is why the HbA1c is important right now. Get the lipid profile and liver function test done as well, given the jaundice history and herbal use. Come back in one week with all reports and we will fine-tune everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please come in and sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Good morning doctor. Umm, I am a homemaker but I also do part-time work at a construction site nearby, handling materials and such.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. What has brought you here today? What is the main problem?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, two days ago I had some kind of incident at the site and after that incident I am having headache and dizziness every few days. Also my arm is feeling numb on one side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Can you describe the headache? Is it shooting type, or more like a dull ache?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, it is shooting type, starting from the back of my neck and going up to the forehead. Very bad it is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any numbness or tingling in the fingers or toes? And do you have any shoulder pain also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, the numbness is there in the right hand fingers, and yes, shoulder pain on the right side is also bothering me since last week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: At the construction site, are you exposed to any chemicals or fumes? Do you come near dogs or animals there?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, there are chemicals used for waterproofing and paint work. And there are stray dogs that roam around the site, I am there daily near them only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you taken anti-rabies vaccination? Any previous vaccination history for rabies or tetanus?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I had vaccination done years back, but I am not sure which one exactly. Also doctor, I had knee replacement done two years ago and hip replacement also three years back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Understood. Do you have sugar problem or blood pressure issue?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have diabetes and I am on medicines but my sugar is not coming under control at all. I also have urine problem — burning and frequent urination is there.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What medicines are you currently taking? And do you smoke or drink alcohol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor I am a social smoker, since college only, so roughly for 20 years. I take warfarin for my heart valve problem and also azithromycin was given recently for some chest infection.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Has any doctor done MRI brain or nerve conduction study before for this numbness?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that was done. Only blood sugar test and HbA1c were done last month. The HbA1c was very high, around 10.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your uncontrolled diabetes, the numbness in your fingers, shooting headache, and dizziness, this looks like diabetic peripheral neuropathy combined with possible cervical radiculopathy from the site injury.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what should I do now? And the urine problem and shoulder pain — are they also related?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The urine problem may be a urinary tract infection which is common with uncontrolled diabetes. The shoulder pain at the right shoulder needs a shoulder X-ray to rule out any injury from the site. We will also order a urine culture and MRI brain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing gabapentin for your nerve pain and numbness. Continue your warfarin as before but we need to check your INR since azithromycin can interact with it.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I stop going to the construction site now? And the stray dogs there, is it dangerous?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please avoid chemicals and heavy work at the site until your shoulder pain and dizziness settle. Regarding the dogs, since your vaccination history is unclear, kindly take anti-rabies shots as a precaution. Also, your smoking will worsen the nerve damage, so please try to stop.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will follow all this. One more thing — I am having sleep disturbance also every few days because of the headache at night, so that is also troubling me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The gabapentin should help with both the nerve pain and sleep disturbance. Come back after one week with the MRI brain report, urine culture, INR, and HbA1c results so we can reassess your treatment plan.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arjun! Good to see you again, yaar. How are things going?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor saab, all good on the surface! But you know, I keep coming back to you for a reason.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ha ha, fair enough. So tell me, how is the recovery going after the surgeries? Any new complaints?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the cholecystectomy site is clear now, no issues there. But the hernia repair from last summer — sometimes I feel a mild pull when I lift heavy at the gym.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, good to hear the cholecystectomy site has healed well. That pulling sensation near the hernia repair site — is it often or only on heavy days?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, it happens multiple times a day on training days, doctor. I have been pushing weights again since last month. Also I have been getting this headache often — like almost countless times some weeks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: This headache — is it on one side or all over the head? Any blurring of vision or nausea with it?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It is mostly at the back of the head, doctor, throbbing type. Nah, no blurring or nausea. But it comes in the morning mostly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Tell me about your sugar readings. You were on metformin — are the levels under control now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ugh, that is the issue doctor. I check every morning and the fasting sugar is still going up — since last three weeks it has been above 200. I am continuing metformin as prescribed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And what about your diet? You were supposed to cut down junk. Are you still eating fast food?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh doctor, I am trying but honestly the fast food is still there — post-workout I grab something quick. And yes, I know you will scold me — I also started vaping again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arjun, seriously! How often are you vaping? And are you working in any environment with chemicals or have you been around a sick person recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The vaping is every morning and sometimes post-gym too. About chemicals — the gym recently started using some strong cleaning agents, so maybe. And a teammate had viral fever — he is basically a sick person I trained with.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any sore throat, cough, or shortness of breath — especially from that chemicals exposure at the gym?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, no cough as such. But my throat feels dry and scratchy — chronic thing doctor, probably the vaping.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Right, so that dry scratchy throat is chronic pharyngeal irritation from vaping. And those morning headaches with fasting sugar above 200 — this is uncontrolled hyperglycemia causing vascular tension, Arjun.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: So the headache is from the sugar? I doubt it is something more serious, right doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The headache is most likely from the uncontrolled hyperglycemia. To rule out other causes we will do a HbA1c, fasting blood glucose, and a blood pressure check today. We also need to revisit your hernia repair site with an ultrasound abdomen given that pulling.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Should I continue metformin alone or do you think we need to add something, doctor?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We are upgrading your regimen, Arjun. I am adding glimepiride 1 mg with dinner, and we will start sitagliptin 50 mg once daily. Continue metformin 500 mg twice daily as before. For the headache, take paracetamol 500 mg as needed for now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And for the gym — can I continue lifting or should I rest the abdomen more?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: No heavy abdomen loading — no deadlifts or weighted squats until the ultrasound abdomen report is clear. The vaping must stop completely — it is worsening your chronic pharyngeal irritation and affecting your blood sugar control. Cut the fast food too — your sugar will never settle otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will get the HbA1c and ultrasound abdomen done this week and come back.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good. Come back in two weeks with the reports. Watch the fasting sugar every morning and note it down — I want to see the trend. Take care of yourself, Arjun — you are young, the body will respond well if you cooperate!

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Welcome back. Good to see you up and about. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am still not feeling fully okay. Last night I had confusion again, like my head was not clear at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any difficulty swallowing also? And is the confusion happening often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Confirmed, doctor, the difficulty swallowing is there intermittently, especially in the mornings. And yes, the confusion is troubling me three times a week at least.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any burning sensation or pain when passing urine? Are you suspecting a UTI?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there is burning pain when I urinate. It started about a week ago. Could be UTI, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Were any tests done during your hospitalisation? Did they run a COVID test or any blood work?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: That's right, they did a COVID test and full blood work when I was admitted. The COVID result came back positive but they said it was a mild strain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned you were on warfarin before. Are you still taking that, and any other medicines currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I am taking warfarin and atorvastatin as before. I also took some OTC medicine from the medical shop for the UTI symptoms, I did not know what else to do.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You should not be taking random OTC medicine especially when you are on warfarin. It can interact badly and affect your blood clotting seriously. Please avoid that going forward.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I understand, doctor. Also, I should mention, there were some insect bites on my arms and legs around the time I fell sick. Could that have triggered something?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is worth noting. Any rash or swelling after those insect bites? And did you develop fever soon after?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes, there was fever and mild rash on my chest. That was around 2024 start of the year when everything began.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I need to ask you something directly. Are you drinking alcohol? How long has this been going on?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... doctor, look, I have been drinking alcohol for 20 years. I know I am young but it started early. My father also was drinking for 30 years, so it is in the family I suppose.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you doing any physical activity like walking or any exercise at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: True, I do walking 3 times a week, but since the hospitalisation I have been resting more. The fatigue is too much after that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on everything — the positive COVID test, the confusion, fatigue, difficulty swallowing, and the timeline — this is a case of post-COVID long-viral sequelae, and additionally you have developed a UTI which needs immediate treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what does long-viral sequelae mean exactly? Is it serious? And the UTI — can it affect my kidneys if left untreated?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It means your body is still recovering from the COVID infection. The confusion and fatigue are part of that. Yes, an untreated UTI can travel upward and affect the kidneys, so we act on it right away.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing nitrofurantoin for the UTI. Continue your warfarin and atorvastatin as before, but I will monitor the warfarin dosing carefully given the new antibiotic. Stop the self-prescribed OTC medicine immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I stop the walking for now? And what about the drinking alcohol — will it make things worse?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Light walking three times a week is fine, but avoid overexerting yourself. As for drinking alcohol, it will absolutely worsen the confusion, interfere with warfarin, and slow your recovery. You must reduce it seriously.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will repeat the blood work in two weeks to check your clotting levels and kidney function. If the difficulty swallowing or confusion worsens before then, come back immediately without waiting.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good afternoon, please sit. What brings you to the chest specialist today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have been having this wheezing and breathlessness since a couple of months now. Also some cough that is comes and goes. My general doctor just sent me here without explaining anything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Is the wheezing happening every night or only during certain activities?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly every night it disturbs my sleep, and a few times during the day also. But honestly I feel the previous doctor was just guessing, so I am not sure this is even a lung problem.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your concern. Have you recently travelled to any rural or congested area? Any mold or pet dander exposure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I visited a relative's old house in a village last month — very damp walls, so maybe mold was there. And they had two cats, so pet dander also. But I doubt this alone caused everything.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any occupational lead exposure or living near industrial areas?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not anymore, doctor. I used to work near a battery manufacturing unit about five years back, but I left that job. Why are you asking all this? Is this really necessary?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is very much necessary, madam. Do you also have joint pain or any cramping sensation anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Actually yes, there is joint pain in my upper part — shoulders mostly. And sometimes this cramping feeling in the intestine area. I have been taking painkillers on my own for that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any issue near the gallbladder area — like pain after eating or bloating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, almost never doctor. Only occasionally. But what does my gallbladder have to do with my breathing? You are checking too many things at once.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Everything is connected, madam. Do you have any history of stroke or elevated blood pressure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had a stroke about three years ago — minor one they said. And still my blood pressure reading comes high sometimes. I take my tablet for it but not regularly, I admit.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink wine or use tobacco? Any screen time habits that affect your sleep?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I have wine every day — just one glass, nothing wrong with that. I am vegetarian so my diet is fine. And yes, my screen time is also quite high at night, but what does that have to do with wheezing?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any smoking history?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I used to smoke half a pack a day for about ten years but quit two years ago. I doubt my old smoking is still causing this after so long.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Madam, based on your mold, pet dander, and prior smoking history combined with every night wheezing and breathlessness, this is a case of allergic asthma with possible chronic obstructive pulmonary disease overlap. The joint pain and lead exposure history also need evaluation for systemic inflammation.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I doubt it doctor, I really feel it could be something else entirely. Are you sure you are not jumping to conclusions?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your scepticism, but we need tests to confirm. I am ordering a PET scan for the systemic inflammation concern and an angiogram given your stroke history and uncontrolled blood pressure. We will also do spirometry and allergy skin testing for the wheezing.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Fine. But what will you give me for now? I cannot keep suffering with this breathlessness every night and this joint pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am starting you on prednisolone for five days to reduce the airway inflammation, along with a bronchodilator inhaler to use when the wheezing gets worse at night. Please stop self-medicating with painkillers as they can worsen asthma.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, please avoid going near damp areas or pet dander exposure again, reduce your wine intake as alcohol can trigger wheezing, and cut down on screen time at night to allow proper sleep and let your blood pressure stabilise.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, but for the joint pain and the cramping near my intestine — will the prednisolone handle that also, or do I need to see some other specialist?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arjun! Good to see you up and about. How is your mother doing? She had called me last week, quite worried about you.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: She is fine doctor, thank you. She has been fussing over me non-stop since the hospital discharge. You know how she is.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Ha, that is what mothers do. So tell me, how are you feeling now after coming home? Any new complaints since discharge?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, last night I had this headache again, very sharp pain on the head. And this morning also I felt dizziness when I got up from bed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, okay. Is the headache comes and goes type, or is it there all the time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It comes and goes, doctor. But this morning it was happening multiple times a day. Very disturbing it was.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any numbness or tingling? Especially in the wrist or fingers area — you had mentioned that in hospital also.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, the wrist is still giving problem. Sometimes there is numbness going up to the arm. It is quite sharp pain at times.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Now I also see in your hospital file that they found fatty liver on the ultrasound. Did you know about this before, or is it a new finding?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, they told me in hospital only doctor. I had no idea. Is it very serious? They used big words and I got confused.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Fatty liver simply means extra fat is getting deposited in your liver. It is not an emergency right now, but we must take it seriously and manage it. Think of it like fat slowly building up where it should not be.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh okay, I understand now. Doctor, also when I was younger I had some breathing problem and they told my family I had COPD. But since I stopped smoking I feel much better on that side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you mentioned COPD. Are you still smoking? And any drinking habits?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Smoking is not anymore, doctor. I used to be a social smoker in college only. Drinking I am an occasional drinker, maybe once a month with friends.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good on the smoking. But even occasional alcohol can worsen fatty liver, so I would strongly advise you to stop that completely. Your liver needs rest right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, in the hospital they also mentioned something about a fistula. I did not understand what that means at all. Is it related to my current problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: A fistula is basically an abnormal connection between two body parts that should not be connected. In your case it was noted as a separate finding. It is not directly causing your headache or dizziness, but we need to monitor it separately.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: One more thing — did you do any international travel in the months before this episode started? Sometimes certain infections are picked up that way.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor! I had done international travel to Thailand for a college trip about three months back. Could that be the cause?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is very helpful information. Looking at everything — your headache, dizziness, numbness in the wrist and arm, the travel history, and your hospital reports — this appears to be a case of viral encephalitis with peripheral nerve involvement. The fatty liver is a separate metabolic finding.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Viral en... what doctor? Is it very dangerous? Should I be scared?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not panic. It simply means a virus caused some swelling inside your brain, and your body is now recovering. We will do a MRI brain and a nerve conduction study for the wrist numbness, and also a liver function test to track the fatty liver.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing acyclovir tablets for the viral infection, betahistine for the dizziness, and vitamin B12 supplements to help with the numbness in your wrist. For the headache, take paracetamol as needed, no strong pain-killers.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I will take all medicines. Anything else I should be careful about? Like for college and all?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rest is very important — no late nights, no alcohol, no travel for now. Eat light food for the fatty liver. If the headache becomes sharp pain again multiple times a day, come immediately. We will review after the MRI brain report comes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please come in, sit down. What has brought you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am having very severe pain in my lower abdomen since two weeks ago. It is becoming too much to bear now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How many months pregnant are you, and is this pain in the lower abdomen constant or does it come and go?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am seven months along doctor. The pain is there sometimes, not all the time. It gets better when I lie on my left side.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bleeding from down below? Any discharge or leaking of water?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, no bleeding doctor, but I did notice some discharge that was slightly yellowish quite a while ago. Now it has mostly stopped.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any headache, blurring of vision, or swelling in the hands and feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My feet are swollen doctor, yes. And sometimes I get headache also, but I thought it was just weakness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any antenatal checkups since the pregnancy started? Any blood pressure monitoring done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor we are very poor, we cannot afford too many visits. I had one checkup since 2024 when the pregnancy was confirmed, that is all. No money for more tests.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand. Any kidney problem, hypertension, or diabetes before this pregnancy?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like that. No such history in family also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? I need you to be honest with me, it is important for your baby's health.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... doctor I used to drink, but never heavily. I stopped after I found out about the pregnancy. I did not want to harm the baby.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any birds at home or nearby? Or any other animal contact that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: We have pigeons on our terrace, yes doctor. There are many birds there. Why are you asking about that?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I will explain shortly. Is the pain also near the intestine area? Any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, sometimes it feels like it is deep inside near the intestine. I have had nausea also but I thought that is normal in pregnancy only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Looking at your swelling, your headache, and this lower abdomen pain, I believe this is a case of preeclampsia. I have ruled out a simple urinary tract infection for now, but we need urgent tests.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Preeclampsia? Doctor, what is that? Is my baby okay? Please tell me, I am very worried.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is a dangerous blood pressure complication in pregnancy. We need to do urine protein test, CBC, liver function test, and an obstetric ultrasound right away. We must monitor the baby closely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am starting you on labetalol for controlling your blood pressure and magnesium sulphate injection to prevent any seizures. You will also need calcium supplements and low dose aspirin as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, these medicines — are they available in the government hospital? I truly cannot afford private pharmacy rates. We have no money at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry, these are all available free at the government hospital. I am referring you there immediately. You must not delay or the preeclampsia can progress to eclampsia with fits, which is very dangerous for both you and the baby. Also, absolutely never take any alcohol again, not even a little.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor, I understand. Thank you so much. I will go right away with my husband.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please come in and have a seat. I understand your family was quite insistent on bringing you today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my wife dragged me here honestly. I told her it is nothing serious but she would not listen.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Well, she did the right thing. Now tell me, what has been happening? Any swelling or discomfort you have noticed?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor, since yesterday my legs are looking quite puffy, especially near the ankles. And two days ago I noticed the swelling had also come near my jaw area, which really scared me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, that puffiness near the jaw and ankles is something we must take seriously. Are you having any breathlessness or chest pain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Not really, doctor. Breathing is mostly fine. But I do feel very fatigue after even small walking — this is almost never like this for me, I am a constable, I walk all day on duty.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any reduced urine output? Or foamy urine? And any nausea or vomiting?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, now that you ask — urine has been less since yesterday also, and it looks a bit frothy. Nausea was there few days ago but that has gone now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you have any history of diabetes or hypertension? And are you on any medicines currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have hypothyroidism — it was detected three years back. I am taking medicines for that. And blood pressure also is slightly high, my previous doctor gave me losartan for that. I also sometimes take tramadol for my back pain because duty is very demanding.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How often are you taking the tramadol? And were you given dexamethasone at any point, maybe for any allergy or inflammation?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Tramadol I take once in a while — not regularly. And yes! Few days ago one colleague gave me dexamethasone saying it will reduce the swelling fast. I took it two or three times only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. Do you smoke or drink alcohol? And what about your diet — are you eating lot of salty or oily food?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker doctor, I smoke only socially at gatherings. Alcohol I have once in a while. But diet is not good honestly — canteen food, very oily, salty, whatever is available on duty.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you posted near any industrial area or mine? Heavy metals sometimes affect the kidneys.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I was posted near a mine area for almost two years before this posting. I was not knowing this can cause kidney issues.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me — the swelling, foamy urine, reduced urine output, and your history of hypertension plus the mine exposure and irregular use of tramadol and dexamethasone — I am suspecting chronic kidney disease. We need to confirm with tests urgently.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Kidney disease? Doctor, that is serious no? I am only forty two. What tests will you do?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I understand this is worrying, but we caught it now and that is good. I will order a TSH because of your hypothyroidism, a serum creatinine and urine albumin test for the kidneys, a X-ray chest to check for fluid accumulation, and an echocardiogram to see if the heart is under any strain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, so many tests. Doctor, this dexamethasone I took — did it make things worse? And should I stop the losartan also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, welcome back. Please sit down comfortably.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Actually, umm, I am a bit nervous. I missed my last few appointments, I apologize for that. I was not feeling too well and work was very hectic.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is alright. Just tell me what is troubling you now. What are your main complaints?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I have been having fever continuously since a few days now and also body ache all over. Yesterday it became very bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is the fever mild or high grade? Any headache or rash on the body?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Uhh, it is mild in the morning but high at night. And yes, headache is there nonstop, radiating from my forehead to the back of my neck. No big rash that I noticed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any vomiting or nausea? What about stomach pain — is it worse after eating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yep, the nausea is there most of the time. And the stomach pain does become worse after eating, especially at night after my shift meal. I do night shifts so I eat very late.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Do you work around any chemicals or pollution in your workplace? Any exposure to cold weather outside?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, not chemicals exactly. But the hospital corridor where I work has a lot of pollution from outside air coming in, and I do walk out in the cold weather at odd hours. Night shifts are quite cold.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of childhood illness like typhoid or dengue before? Do you have high blood pressure or thyroid disorder?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had some childhood illness — my mother told me it was typhoid when I was around seven. And I was also detected with thyroid disorder two years back. I also have high blood pressure but that is somewhat controlled now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you on any medications currently for thyroid disorder or high blood pressure?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I was on levothyroxine and amlodipine but I am no longer taking them regularly. I kept skipping doses because of the night shift schedule.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see, that is a concern. Do you smoke or drink wine? Any regular exercise or sports?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, I used to play sports — football — but not anymore. I drink wine occasionally on weekends. And about smoking — yes, I am a chain smoker, easily a pack a day. I know it is bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any joint pain or eye redness? Any bleeding from the gums or blood in urine?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Nah, nothing like bleeding at all. But joint pain is there in my knees and wrists. I thought it was from long standing during night duty. No eye redness that I noticed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We need to run some tests urgently. I am ordering a dengue NS1 antigen test, Widal test for typhoid, complete blood count, and thyroid function test. Also a blood pressure reading right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. Will the dengue NS1 antigen test confirm whether I have dengue? I am a bit scared about that.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms — the continuous fever, headache, joint pain, and nausea — this looks like a probable case of dengue fever. We cannot rule out typhoid either, given your history. Tests will confirm.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yep, please tell me what I should do now, doctor. Can I continue going to night shifts? I do not want to lose pay.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Absolutely not. You must take complete rest, no night shifts for at least one week. The cold weather exposure at night and irregular sleep are making the fever worse. Drink plenty of fluids, especially water and coconut water. Avoid wine and smoking completely during this illness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing paracetamol 500 mg three times a day for fever and body ache, ondansetron for the nausea, and ORS sachets to stay hydrated. Also restart your levothyroxine and amlodipine from today itself — skipping those is not acceptable.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will take the medicines properly this time and come back once the test results are ready. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please sit down comfortably. What is your name, son?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am Rohan, doctor. I am 16 years old. My parents sent me here for some surgery clearance check.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright Rohan, before we do the pre-operative clearance, I need to understand your general health. What is bothering you these days? Any pain or discomfort anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, umm, I have been having shoulder pain on the lower part of my shoulder and also some heaviness near the spleen area and navel area. It is very uncomfortable, doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, that is quite a few areas. Is this shoulder pain sharp or more like a dull ache? And since when?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: It started this morning very suddenly, but the heaviness near the spleen side has been there for a couple of days now. It is paining constantly, not going away at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any nausea, vomiting, or fever along with this? And have you had any bleeding or loose motion?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, no fever doctor, but I did have nausea a few times since 10-15 days. And my stomach feels bloated too.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rohan, I want to ask you something and I need you to be honest with me, okay? Do you drink alcohol? There is no judgment here.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, doctor please don't tell my parents, but yes, I have been drinking. My friends started it and I got into it. I have been doing it for 10 years... uh wait no, I mean, I know I am only 16, I started very young, maybe 3 years.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand, Rohan. It takes courage to share that. Do you also use tobacco in any form? And are you doing any running or physical exercise regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did try tobacco a couple of times, doctor. And yes, I do running for school sports. But lately the shoulder pain and navel area heaviness is stopping me from exercising.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you had any recent hospital visit or exposure to birds or any animals? And any past fracture or surgery?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I had a fracture in my left arm two years back, that is why surgery is planned now. And there was one hospital visit last month for chest pain but they said nothing serious. We also have birds at home, pigeons actually.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Are you taking any medicines on your own for this pain? Any painkillers from the pharmacy without prescription?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. I have been taking ibuprofen and sometimes antacid tablets on my own. I did not tell anyone. The ibuprofen helps a few times but then the pain comes back near my navel area constantly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any yellowing of your eyes or skin? Any weight loss recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, my mother did say my eyes looked a little yellow couple of days ago. And I have lost some weight I think, my clothes feel loose. There is also itching on my skin sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rohan, based on what you are telling me, we need to do a few tests urgently. I am ordering a liver function test, complete blood count, abdominal ultrasound, and a chest X-ray also, given your history of chest pain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, is this serious? Why would my spleen be hurting and why the yellowing? I am really scared now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Rohan, I want to be honest with you gently. The combination of jaundice, the heaviness near the spleen, nausea, and your alcohol use is pointing strongly towards alcoholic hepatitis with possible early liver damage. The ibuprofen you are self-taking is also making the stomach lining worse.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, will I be able to have the surgery for my fracture repair? And what should I do now? I am very worried, I do not want my parents to be upset.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The surgery for the fracture will have to be postponed until your liver function stabilizes — surgery under liver damage conditions is very risky. You must stop all alcohol immediately and stop the self-medication with ibuprofen completely. Your parents will need to know, but I will speak to them kindly alongside you.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: For now I am prescribing ursodeoxycholic acid tablets to support liver function, pantoprazole for your stomach lining, and multivitamin syrup with zinc supplements to help with your weight loss and nutritional deficit. Absolutely no ibuprofen or any NSAIDs from here on.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor for not being harsh. I will follow everything. I just hope the shoulder pain and the navel area pain also get better soon. I promise I will stop alcohol and tobacco completely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Very good attitude, Rohan. You must also rest completely, stop running or any strenuous exercise until your liver function test reports come back normal. Avoid any birds contact at home as respiratory infections can worsen your recovery. Come back in 10-15 days for repeat blood work and we will reassess the surgery plan.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Arrey, Suresh! Come come, sit down. How is your wife? And the kids — exams are going on, no?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, all fine. Wife is managing the house. Younger one's school exams are there next week. But I myself am still not hundred percent, that is why I came so soon.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you came early for follow-up. You were discharged not too long ago, so I want to check everything properly. How are you feeling overall?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the fever has reduced, but I am still feeling moderate weakness. Body is not cooperating fully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any rash on the body? Or any skin infection anywhere? Sometimes after such fever it can appear.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes doctor, there is something near my belly button area — some redness there. I thought it was just irritation from the hospital bed.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me see — yes, this looks like a skin infection, possibly secondary to your hospital stay. We need to address this. And your blood pressure reading — let me do a BP check right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, the blood pressure was always slightly high, from long time now. Even in hospital they were noting it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Now, I heard from the discharge nurse you were on medicines from two or three different doctors. What all are you taking currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor. One doctor near our locality gave me clopidogrel for the heart thinning. Another doctor gave acetaminophen for pain and fever. And pregabalin was given for some nerve pain in my legs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Suresh, this is a problem. Clopidogrel and acetaminophen together can affect your stomach lining, and with dengue history your platelet count was already low. You should not take these without telling me first.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am sorry doctor, I did not know. Also, I have diabetes and asthma from long time, so different doctors have been giving different things.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. What about cold weather — does it trigger your breathlessness? And any cats or animals at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, cold weather definitely makes my breathlessness worse. And we do have two cats at home, they are with us from long time. You think they are causing problem?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Possibly contributing to your asthma. I want to arrange an allergy test for you — it will show if the cats are a trigger. Also, we had done a PSA test during your admission as routine screening — that report is here, it looks absent for any concern, so no prostate issue right now.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Oh that is a relief doctor. And the dengue and typhoid both together — is that common? I had both confirmed in hospital only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is uncommon but not impossible, especially when the body immunity is weak. Your measles history as a child also may have left some effect on immunity. That is why recovery is slower for you.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also do cycling and running for fitness — for 20 years I have been doing this. Should I continue now or stop?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Stop running and heavy cycling for at least two to three weeks. Your body is still recovering. Also, I know you take coffee — do you have it socially or more regularly?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I take coffee socially mostly, but occasionally at home also when work stress is there. At the tailor shop, long hours sitting also giving me back pain occasionally.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any nausea or vomiting still? And loose motion — is it there or absent now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The loose motion is absent now, thankfully. Nausea is also gone mostly. Only the weakness and that belly button area redness is bothering me.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright Suresh, I am stopping clopidogrel for now — do not take it until I review. Continue acetaminophen only if fever comes, not otherwise. For the skin infection near belly button, I am prescribing a topical antibiotic cream. Hold pregabalin also — I will re-evaluate that nerve pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also, keep monitoring your blood pressure with home BP check every morning. Note down the readings and bring them when you come next week. We will also recheck your dengue recovery with a blood panel.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. I will note the BP check readings occasionally — I mean morning and evening both. And I will not start cycling or running without asking you. Thank you so much doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Hello, come in, come in. Please have a seat. I see this is a referral visit — what brings you here today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am a 15-year-old girl. My periods have been extremely painful and irregular since the last six months, and I also have this discharge that is bothering me all the time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Is the pain in the lower abdomen or anywhere near the epigastric region also?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Mostly lower abdomen doctor, but sometimes it goes up near the epigastric area and feels unbearable. I read online it could be PCOS or even endometriosis.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any acne on the face or back? Any unusual hair fall or weight gain?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Present, yes doctor — lots of acne on my face and there is also hair fall three times a week I notice big clumps in the shower. The internet said these are classic PCOS signs.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any tenderness or swelling in the breast area? And is the discharge warm or foul-smelling?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the breast area is slightly sore, yes. And the discharge — it is warm and yellowish. Doctor, I also developed a skin infection on my thigh last month and it has not fully gone.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was that skin infection after a mosquito bite or any other pesticides contact? Do you live near farmland?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I think there was a mosquito bite first, then it got infected. We do live near fields so pesticides exposure is possible, but I am not aware of any direct contact.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of food allergy? And are you currently on any medicines — like OTC medicine or cough syrup for anything?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I have a food allergy to shellfish. And I was taking some OTC medicine for sinusitis two weeks back. Also a cough syrup my mother gave me when I had a cold.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Was the sinusitis also accompanied by facial pain or nasal discharge? And how often?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, doctor, facial pain and blocked nose — it keeps coming back three times a week when weather changes. I read sinusitis can trigger hormonal issues, is that true?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That connection is not so straightforward. Now tell me — do you alcohol drink or smoke at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I drink alcohol occasionally, like 2 drinks a week at parties. I don't think so that it is causing my period problems, but maybe?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It definitely contributes. Have you done any tests earlier — a USG report or albumin level check? And when was your last weight check?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My family doctor did a USG report three months ago and said ovaries looked bulky. Weight check was done then too — I had gained 6 kg. No albumin test was done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on the bulky ovaries on USG report, the acne, hair fall, irregular periods, and weight gain, this is a case of PCOS — Polycystic Ovarian Syndrome. The skin infection and discharge are secondary concerns we will address separately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also read that warfarin can sometimes affect periods — my aunt takes it. Could that be a reason? And can PCOS happen during pregnancy also?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Warfarin affects bleeding patterns but you are not on it, so it is not relevant here. Regarding during pregnancy — PCOS is a pre-existing hormonal condition, it does not newly develop during pregnancy, though it can complicate one.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing combined oral contraceptive pill to regulate your cycle and reduce acne, along with metformin 500 mg for insulin resistance. For the skin infection, I will add topical clindamycin to apply on the thigh area.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please stop the alcohol completely while on metformin — it can cause serious side effects. Also avoid self-medicating with any OTC medicine without asking me first, especially given your food allergy history.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. And what about the sinusitis — should I continue the cough syrup? And do I need another USG report soon?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Stop the cough syrup for now. I will refer you to an ENT for the recurring sinusitis. Yes, repeat USG report, albumin, and a full hormonal panel in four weeks, and come back for weight check monthly so we can track your progress properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good morning, please take a seat. You are here for the insurance medical documentation, correct?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, good morning. My company is asking for a full fitness certificate for long-distance driving. They need detailed records.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright, I will do a thorough check. Tell me, are you having any cough, breathlessness, or wheezing currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, yes, I have been having cough on and off for many months now. Wheezing happens every other day, especially early morning.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any breathlessness while driving or on physical exertion? Any chest tightness or chest pain in the chest area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the breathlessness comes periodically doctor, mostly when I am going up a slope or lifting luggage. There is some chest tightness but no severe chest pain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are you a cigarettes smoker? If yes, how much are you smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I have been smoking cigarettes two packs a day since 2023. Before that also I was smoking, but less.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you ever used opioids or any other substances? This is for the medico-legal record, please be honest.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor I must be honest — I have used opioids periodically in the past for staying awake on long night routes, but I have stopped now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Noted. Any crowded places exposure regularly, like bus depots or busy terminals, which could worsen respiratory symptoms?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, crowded places like bus stands and depots — I am there every other day. Lot of dust and fumes also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you have any past history of high blood pressure, clotting disorder, or jaundice?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I had jaundice when I was young. And they once told me I have some clotting disorder after a leg swelling episode. High blood pressure — no, not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any bluish discolouration of the lips that you or anyone has noticed? Any swelling in the legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: My wife says my lips look slightly bluish sometimes, especially after climbing stairs. Leg swelling I had before but no current swelling.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any bleeding issues or abdominal pain near the colon area? Any loose motions or blood in stool?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, nothing like blood in stool. Some abdominal pain near the colon side occasionally, but I thought it was gas trouble. No bleeding.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any spirometry, chest X-ray, or complete blood count recently? Any treatment going on currently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, I did a chest X-ray 2023 only — they said some hyperinflation was there. No spirometry was done. Currently no medicines, nothing.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your heavy smoking of cigarettes at two packs a day, the wheezing, breathlessness, bluish lips, and hyperinflation on chest X-ray, this is a case of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. The past clotting disorder also makes things complicated.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing a short course of steroids to reduce the airway inflammation, and given your clotting disorder history and risk of deep vein thrombosis, we will add heparin under close supervision. I will also order a spirometry, D-dimer test, and liver function test given your jaundice history before finalising the certificate.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, should I be worried about taking steroids with my clotting disorder? And will these tests affect my fitness certificate outcome?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The steroids dose will be low and short-term, and heparin will protect against clotting risk. You must completely stop cigarettes and opioids — continued use will directly affect your fitness clearance for driving. Avoid crowded places with heavy dust and fumes as much as possible, and report any worsening breathlessness or coughing up blood immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor, thank you. I will get all the tests done and come back as soon as possible.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please take a seat. No need to be nervous.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... thank you doctor. I am having weakness in my arms and legs since 2024. It is getting very bad now.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Tell me, is there any numbness or tingling in the hands or feet?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... yes doctor. Tingling in both feet is there daily. Hands also sometimes go numb.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any muscle pain or cramps? And are you having fatigue even after rest?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, fatigue is very bad. Even after sleeping full night I feel extremely tired. Muscle pain in legs is there about a week more severely.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You mentioned these problems started in 2024. Did you have a COVID infection or some severe viral fever around that time?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... yes doctor. I had COVID in early 2024. After that these weakness and tiredness started only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any past surgery or other serious illness before this?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... I had past surgery on my abdomen some years back for a hernia. Otherwise nothing serious doctor.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. You are a manual labourer — any animal hair exposure at your worksite? And do you live in a rural area?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I work near a farm. Animal hair is always there. I am from a rural area only. Sometimes we eat outside and food quality is not good — contaminated food also possible.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink alcohol? And are you taking any opioids or any other medicines on your own?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm... doctor I take alcohol 2 drinks a week only. About opioids... I was taking some pain tablets for the muscle pain but I stopped.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. I have your lab reports here. Your AST levels are elevated and I had also recommended an EMG. Did you get both done?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor. I got the AST and EMG done last week only. I have the reports here.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Let me review. Your EMG is showing peripheral neuropathy and the elevated AST suggests some liver stress. Combined with your COVID history and exposure, this is a case of post-COVID neuropathy with early hepatic involvement.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh... doctor, this neuropathy — is it very serious? Will I be able to do my work again?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It is manageable if we treat it properly and early. You must stop the opioids completely and reduce alcohol intake as both are worsening your liver stress and nerve damage.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing methylcobalamin for the nerve weakness, pregabalin for the tingling and pain, and silymarin to support your liver.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any foods I should avoid? And the contaminated food issue — should I be more careful?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, absolutely avoid contaminated food. Eat only properly cooked meals. Avoid heavy lifting that strains your arms and legs until the weakness improves. Also limit animal hair contact and wear a mask at the worksite.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, do I need to come back soon? How will you check if I am improving?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, I want a follow-up in four weeks. We will repeat the AST and also do a nerve conduction study to see how the peripheral neuropathy is responding to treatment.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you so much doctor. I will follow everything properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Good to see you back. How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I came for the follow-up after discharge. I had that episode two months ago but these new complaints are there about a week now. headache is still there, mildly uncomfortable but not going.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. And what about the dizziness? Is that also continuing? Any numbness in the arm or the toes?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, dizziness is there. And the numbness in the toes started three days ago. The arm also feels a little dead sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: How often is the dizziness coming? Is it weekly or more frequent than that?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, it is coming weekly at least, doctor. Sometimes two, three times in a week also. When I stand up fast, it is very bad.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. And tell me about your cigarettes. Are you still smoking?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, doctor I know you will scold me. I am a chain smoker for many years. I am trying to reduce but it is very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: You must stop completely, no negotiation on that. What about your sleep habits? Are you sleeping properly at night? And are you doing any swimming or any exercise?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, sleep is very poor. I am getting only three, four hours. And swimming I am doing 1 hour daily in the morning but about a week back I stopped because of the dizziness.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good that you stopped for now. Any sun exposure for long hours? Or any animal hair contact at home?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I sit outside on the terrace in the afternoon. So sun exposure is there daily. And we have a cat at home, so animal hair is everywhere in the house.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. When you were admitted, we did a CT scan brain and a MRI brain. Did you bring those reports today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, I brought them. See, doctor. But I am a poor man, I cannot afford all these big tests again. Please see what is manageable.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand your situation completely. Looking at the reports and your symptoms, this is a case of transient ischemic attack with residual cervical spondylosis changes. The numbness in the toes and arm is from nerve compression, and the dizziness and headache are from reduced blood flow to the brain.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, what does that mean exactly? Is it serious? I am worried because I had a mild stroke two months ago also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It means we must be very careful. I am prescribing aspirin 75 mg once daily, atorvastatin 40 mg at night, and amlodipine 5 mg in the morning for your hypertension. Also continue the physiotherapy exercises for the neck and arm.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, these medicines, all are expensive? I am struggling financially. Is there any cheaper option in the government hospital?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do not worry. Aspirin and atorvastatin are available in generic form at the Jan Aushadhi centre, very cheap. I will write generic names only. Also, please do a blood pressure monitoring every week and a fasting blood sugar test also, since high sugar can worsen your condition.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now, very important — avoid sun exposure in the afternoon completely. The cigarettes must stop today, because smoking is directly worsening the blood supply to your brain. Also the animal hair from the cat — if you are getting any sneezing or breathing difficulty, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Understood doctor. No sneezing or breathing difficulty from the cat. But I will keep the cat outside now only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Good decision. Also fix your sleep habits — at least seven hours of rest is needed. You can restart swimming after two more weeks, slowly, only 1 hour daily, and check your dizziness before getting in the water. Do not go alone.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Now I want to do a teach-back. Can you tell me — what three medicines did I give you, and when to take them?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ji doctor. You gave me aspirin in the morning, atorvastatin at night, and amlodipine in the morning also. And I must not go in the sun exposure and must stop cigarettes fully.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Excellent, very good! You remembered everything correctly. Come back in ten days. If numbness in the arm or toes increases, or if vision blurring or speech difficulty comes, go to emergency immediately, do not wait. We will repeat the MRI brain after three months if things are not improving.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit quickly, I have many patients today.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Sorry doctor. I am feeling very tired and dizzy for a year now. Last few days it became very bad, that is why I came.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any breathlessness or palpitations? Any yellowing of your eyes or skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, breathlessness is there nonstop since few days. And yellowing of eyes, my wife noticed last week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any headache or fainting? How about swelling in legs?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Headache is there every morning, doctor. Swelling in legs is also there intermittently. No fainting but I feel I will fall sometimes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any history of bleeding disorders or high blood pressure in the family?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, not aware of any such thing in family, doctor. I myself had high blood pressure detected last year only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any known drug allergy? And are you currently on any blood pressure tablets?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No allergy doctor. I was on amlodipine but I stopped it on my own and started some ayurvedic tablet from the medical shop last month.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
