utterances.text: Doctor: You changed medicine on your own? That is not correct. Do you drink alcohol or smoke?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, sorry doctor. Yes I drink alcohol, 3 beers a day, for 10 years. I also smoke every morning with my tea, one cigarette only.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: What work do you do? Any factory exposure or pollution?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am daily-wage labourer doctor, I work in a factory near the highway. Lot of pollution and dust there. No mask or anything they give us.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Did you do any tests before coming? Any USG report or Echo done before the tests I will prescribe?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I did one ultrasound last month doctor, at a small clinic. They said liver is slightly enlarged but I did not understand the report properly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Looking at your tiredness, yellowing of eyes, swelling, and your alcohol history, this is a case of anaemia with nutritional deficiency and possible liver damage.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Anaemia means what doctor? Is it very serious?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Anaemia means your blood is very low in iron and important nutrients. With your alcohol intake and factory work, your body is not absorbing properly. It can become serious if ignored.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing ferrous sulphate tablet every morning after food, folic acid once daily, and restart your amlodipine for high blood pressure. Stop that ayurvedic tablet immediately.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Okay doctor. This tiredness in legs and dizziness will go with these medicines?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It will improve in four to six weeks if you take medicines properly. You must also eat green vegetables, lentils, and eggs every morning. Your breathlessness and swelling should reduce as anaemia improves.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Reduce your alcohol intake immediately — your liver is already showing enlargement. Smoking also must stop. Never change your blood pressure medication on your own again.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am ordering a fresh ultrasound, an Echo for your heart given the swelling, and a full blood count with liver function test. Bring all reports next week.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor, I will do all tests and come. I will try to reduce drinking also.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. Please sit down. How are you doing today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am not doing well at all. My knee is paining extremely painful... and I also have been feeling very tired and yellow looking just started this week.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, what brings you here today — is it a refill visit or something new coming up?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, mainly refill, doctor. I am on metformin and levothyroxine since 2023. But I delayed coming — I was caught up with college exams for weeks.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Alright. You mentioned knee pain — which knee is it, and is the area warm or swollen?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Right knee, doctor. It is warm to touch and feels thick inside. I have had this pain several times this month but I kept ignoring it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Is there any jaundice — any yellowing of your eyes or skin?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my friends noticed my eyes are a bit yellow. I also feel very pale. Could it be anemia?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Possibly. Are you having any fatigue, breathlessness, or dizziness along with the pallor?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, dizziness especially when I stand up fast. And fatigue is there several times during the day. I also had jaundice once last summer too.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I see. Any pollen or dust exposure recently? Sometimes allergic reactions can worsen systemic conditions.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, the college campus has a lot of pollen these days doctor, I sneeze a lot. Could that be connected to the jaundice?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Not directly, but let us not ignore it. Now tell me — have you had any check-up done recently for your diabetes and thyroid?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: No doctor, I did a check-up back in 2023 only. Since then no tests done. I also have high cholesterol — the doctor had mentioned it then. And my mother had a mammogram done recently and they said there is family risk so I should watch out.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, good you mentioned that family history. Do you exercise or follow any diet for the cholesterol?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I go for jogging 3 times a week doctor, but diet is very bad — hostel food, lot of fried things. I also skip meals during exam time.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on what you are telling me, you have active anemia, possible jaundice recurrence, and knee pain that looks like joint inflammation — likely worsened by your poorly controlled diabetes and hypothyroidism.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, why does thyroid problem cause all this? I thought it just causes weight gain.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Uncontrolled hypothyroidism can cause anemia, joint pain, fatigue, and even affect your liver slightly, which explains the jaundice picture. Your high cholesterol also goes up when thyroid is low.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am continuing your metformin and increasing the dose of levothyroxine. I am also adding iron supplement for the anemia, atorvastatin for cholesterol, and diclofenac gel for the knee.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, any side effects of atorvastatin? And can I continue jogging with this knee pain?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Avoid jogging for now — rest the knee for at least two weeks. Atorvastatin can rarely cause muscle pain, especially in the legs, so tell me immediately if you feel muscle weakness. Also avoid pollen exposure as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: We will do a complete blood count, liver function test, thyroid stimulating hormone, HbA1c, and lipid profile today. Please do not delay like this again — missing medications for weeks is very risky for your sugar and thyroid.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I also wanted to say — I feel knee pain is extremely painful in the knee joint area in the mornings mainly. Should I do any scan?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Yes, let us also add a X-ray knee today. If it is showing joint swelling, we may need a rheumatoid factor test also. Come back in two weeks with all reports and we will review everything thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Come in, come in. You look a bit pale today — what happened?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I came in just now from the gym, and I am feeling dizzy and breathless. My gums have been bleeding nonstop for the past hour. It is scaring me honestly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay, let me check. Any fatigue, pallor, or palpitations also? You do sports regularly, right?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I play football and do heavy weight training daily. The fatigue has been there on and off but the gum bleeding from the gums is new and the dizziness is worse than usual.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any joint pain, rashes on the skin, or hair fall lately?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: The hair fall is there once in a while, but I attributed it to the gym stress. Joint pain is hardly ever there. No rashes.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you take any supplements or medicines at home? Any cough syrup or over-the-counter stuff recently?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, I was taking a cough syrup last week for a viral. I also take synthroid for my hypothyroidism — been on it for 30 years almost, since childhood diagnosis.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Okay. Any pets at home? And seasonal changes — does all this worsen in winter or summer?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, we have two dogs at home, so pets are there. And honestly, every winter my fatigue and breathlessness get significantly worse. I thought it was just the cold weather affecting my performance.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you smoke or consume cannabis?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I take cannabis socially at parties, not regularly. I do not smoke cigarettes at all.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any blood work recently? Any complete blood count or serum ferritin done before?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had a CBC done three months ago and my haemoglobin was borderline low — around 10.5 — but my trainer said it is fine for endurance athletes. I did not follow up.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any tingling or numbness in the hands or feet? Any mouth ulcers or soreness around the tongue?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, yes actually — some tingling in the fingers once in a while post-workout. And my tongue has been feeling smooth and sore for a few weeks. I did not connect it.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Putting it all together — the gum bleeding, fatigue, pallor, smooth tongue, tingling in the fingers, and that low haemoglobin — this looks like combined iron deficiency anaemia with vitamin C deficiency, possibly early scurvy. The seasonal worsening fits as well.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Scurvy? I thought that was an old sailor disease, doctor. How is that possible when I eat well and do sports?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: High-intensity athletes actually have higher vitamin C turnover. The pets are not causing it, but combined with seasonal low fruit intake and the stress of heavy training, your stores depleted. The cough syrup has nothing to do with it, but some syrups do affect platelet function mildly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I am prescribing ferrous sulfate 200 mg twice daily with food, vitamin C 500 mg twice daily — this will also help iron absorption — and folic acid 5 mg once daily. We will hold heparin for now as there is active gum bleeding and we do not want to thin the blood further.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Can I continue my workouts? And should I stop the synthroid or take it at a different time with these new medicines?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Take synthroid first thing in the morning on empty stomach as usual, and give a gap of at least two hours before the ferrous sulfate — iron interferes with thyroid absorption. Reduce gym intensity for the next two weeks at least, no heavy lifting while the dizziness and bleeding are active.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I want you to get a serum ferritin, vitamin C level, CBC, and TSH done today itself. Also cut down the cannabis — it is not helping your breathlessness or lung capacity with sport.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: How long before I start feeling better, doctor? And the gums — will the bleeding stop soon?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The gum bleeding from the gums should reduce within one week once vitamin C kicks in. The anaemia will take six to eight weeks to correct fully. Come back in four weeks with the reports and we will recheck your haemoglobin. Do not skip the synthroid and increase citrus fruits and green vegetables in your diet starting today.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Please come in and sit down. I understand you are here for documentation purposes today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes doctor, my insurance company is asking for a proper medical certificate. I am an elderly lady living alone, so I need everything properly written down.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Of course, we will take care of that. First tell me, what main complaints are you having? Any stomach pain or acidity?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, for three months I am having stomach pain and cramps in my abdomen, and so much gas trouble also. It is happening many times in the day.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Are these cramps sharp or dull and aching? And any bloating after eating?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Umm, mostly dull and aching doctor, but several times it becomes sharp. Yes, bloating is also there after every meal. And two days ago I had very severe acidity with burning in my chest.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Any nausea or vomiting? And any menstrual bleeding or abnormal bleeding from anywhere?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I am past that age, so no contact with menstrual bleeding for many years now. But nausea is there, true, especially in the mornings.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Do you drink wine or any alcohol? And are you non-vegetarian?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Ahh, yes doctor, I take wine maybe 2 drinks a week only. And yes I am non-vegetarian, I eat chicken and fish regularly. Could that be causing this?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: It can contribute, yes. Now, do you smoke at all?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I am a social smoker doctor, not a regular one. But my son when he visits, he smokes a pack a day inside the house.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: That is passive smoke exposure, which is harmful. Now, any mold in your house? You mentioned you live alone in an old building.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor now that you mention it, there is mold on the walls in my bathroom and kitchen. I have been complaining to the building people but nothing is done.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: And what about screen time? Are you spending long hours on mobile or tablet late at night?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Yes, correct doctor, I do a lot of screen time at night because I cannot sleep. I watch shows until very late, then my stomach starts paining badly.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Have you done any upper GI endoscopy or H. pylori breath test before? Any past history of peptic ulcer disease?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: I had a endoscopy done about five years back, they said mild gastritis at that time. Since then I was taking some antacid syrup but I stopped it on my own.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Based on your symptoms of cramps, bloating, acidity, and the history of gastritis, along with your lifestyle factors, I am diagnosing you with gastroesophageal reflux disease with underlying irritable bowel syndrome. The mold and late-night screen time are making it worse.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, so what exactly is happening in my stomach? Should I be worried?

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: The acid from your stomach is going back up into your food pipe, causing the burning and cramps. The gas trouble and bloating are from the bowel sensitivity. We need to do a stool H. pylori antigen test and a repeat upper GI endoscopy to confirm. Also a complete blood count to check for any anemia.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Doctor, I must tell you honestly, I am on pension only, my budget is very tight. I cannot afford expensive medicines.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: I understand completely. I am prescribing affordable generic medicines for you. Take pantoprazole 40 mg once daily before breakfast, domperidone 10 mg before meals for the nausea and bloating, and simethicone drops for the gas trouble. These are all available at government dispensary at low cost.

utterances.speaker: Doctor
utterances.text: Doctor: Also please reduce your wine intake, stop eating spicy and heavy non-vegetarian food at night, and reduce late-night screen time as it disturbs your digestion and sleep cycle. The mold must be removed — it can worsen your gastric irritation and cause respiratory symptoms too.

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Patient: Thank you doctor. Correct, I will follow everything. Please make the certificate also for the insurance people mentioning my gastroesophageal reflux disease and the tests you have advised.
